title: st.connection(conn_name, type='snowflake') doesn't use named connection.
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary Trying to make a Snowflake connection, as per [example 3](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/connections/st.connections.snowflakeconnection), fails, where a single named connection is available in the `conncetions.toml`. It appears to ignore the named connection, and use the 'default' connection name. Setting the `SNOWFLAKE_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_NAME` environment variable will allow a succesful connection, with the same named connection and same `conncetions.toml` file. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import os import streamlit as st conn_name = os.getenv('SNOWFLAKE_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_NAME') st.write(conn_name) # None conn_name = 'EQSQTDL-RG49312' st.write(conn_name) # EQSQTDL-RG49312 try: conn = st.connection(conn_name, type='snowflake') st.success('Connected using conn_name.') except: st.warning('conn_name failed!') os.environ['SNOWFLAKE_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_NAME'] = 'EQSQTDL-RG49312' conn_name = os.getenv('SNOWFLAKE_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_NAME') conn = st.connection('snowflake') st.success('Connected using named default connection.') ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Configure a connections.toml file with valid connection parameters. 2. Run the above app. ### Expected Behavior App should write success message "Connected using conn_name" ### Current Behavior ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.57.0 - Python version: 3.12.10 - Operating System: Windows - Browser: Edge ### Additional Information _No response_

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15353)

Hey, I was just studying the st.connection routing and tracked down this bug. The fallback _connect logic drops the connection_name argument when secrets.toml is empty. I have a fix ready and am opening a PR momentarily to inject the name back into the kwargs..

### Issue Analysis

This bug reports that `st.connection("my_connection", type="snowflake")` ignores the connection name passed by the user and instead tries to use the `default` entry from `~/.snowflake/connections.toml` (which fails when no `default` entry exists). Setting the `SNOWFLAKE_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_NAME` environment variable works around the problem, confirming that the named connection is never forwarded to `snowflake.connector.connect()`.

### Likely Root Cause

In [`lib/streamlit/connections/snowflake_connection.py`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/connections/snowflake_connection.py), the `SnowflakeConnection._connect` method handles three cases:

1. If Streamlit secrets exist → use them.
2. If `self._connection_name == "snowflake"` → call `snowflake.connector.connect()` with no args (relies on Snowflake's default-connection logic).
3. Otherwise → call `snowflake.connector.connect(**kwargs)`.

```619:663:lib/streamlit/connections/snowflake_connection.py
    def _connect(self, **kwargs: Any) -> InternalSnowflakeConnection:
        ...
        st_secrets = self._secrets.to_dict()
        try:
            if len(st_secrets):
                ...
                conn_kwargs = {**st_secrets, **kwargs}
                return snowflake.connector.connect(**conn_kwargs)

            if self._connection_name == "snowflake":
                ...
                return snowflake.connector.connect()

            return snowflake.connector.connect(**kwargs)
```

In case 3 (the user's scenario, e.g. `st.connection("EQSQTDL-RG49312", type="snowflake")` with no matching `[connections.<name>]` block in `secrets.toml`), `self._connection_name` is never forwarded to the Snowflake connector. The connector therefore falls back to its own default (`"default"`), which is exactly the behavior the user describes. The fix is to pass `connection_name=self._connection_name` (when no secrets are configured and the name is not `"snowflake"`) so that Snowflake resolves the matching entry in `~/.snowflake/connections.toml`. This also matches the documented Example 3 in the `SnowflakeConnection` docstring.

### Related Issues

- [#9016 — Cannot Use kwargs Only in Snowflake Connection](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9016): Another bug in the same `_connect` branching logic — when secrets are absent, the call path doesn't behave as documented. Likely fixable alongside this one.
- [#7637 — SnowflakeConnection.query() retries on errors that will never succeed](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7637): Same `SnowflakeConnection` class; useful context for connection-establishment behavior, though not a duplicate.
- [#8381 — Connection for duckdb](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8381): General `feature:connections` request, only loosely related (different connector, but same module).
